newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ median house price falls 1.2 pct in April-REINZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ median house price falls 1.2 pct in April-REINZ.

text.p: The national median house price fell 1.2 percent to NZ$162,500 in April from $164,000 in March, the Real Estate Institute of New Zealand (REINZ) said on Wednesday.
On an annual basis, the median was up 9.1 percent from $149,000 a year ago.
In Auckland, the median house price rose 0.4 percent to $236,000 from $235,000 in March and $229,000 in April last year.

REINZ national vice-president Max Oliver said there was some weakening in market confidence in April, due mainly to the uncertainty over mortgage interest rate stability which prevailed over the month.
"The interesting thing will be to see if May figures show any benefit from recent mortgage interest rate reductions," Oliver said.
The total number of home sales dipped slightly in April to 8,080 down from 8,219 in March but up from 7,815 in January and 8,033 in February.
While the number of homes sold fell in the year to April, their value rose to NZ$1.55 billion from $1.52 billion in April 1996.
House sales in Auckland totalled 2,730 in April, down from 2,852 in March and 2,857 in April 1996.
The number of home sales also dipped slightly in Wellington (down 23 to 1,025) and Canterbury (down 33 to 1,246).
